probes.question: Why could an AC system reach farther than Edison's low-voltage DC?
options: It used transformers to step high voltage down for use

probes.question: True or false: Edison's first utility was based on DC power.

image.alt: A large hydroelectric power plant building beside blue water on the Niagara River, seen from the bank.

panels.text: 1882. Thomas Edison establishes the first investor-owned electric utility, built on direct current (DC).
Low-voltage DC had a short useful range. To keep costly copper conductors small, plants had to sit in the middle of population centres and could only supply customers less than a mile away.

In 1886 George Westinghouse's company introduces alternating current (AC), using transformers to step high voltage down for indoor lighting. High voltage let power travel farther from large central stations.
AC won. Westinghouse took the major part of the Niagara Falls hydroelectric contract in 1893, and DC utility systems declined through the 20th century.
